strategy.summary: The orders detail scenario (GET /orders/:id) slowed from p95 22 ms to 30 ms and p99 23 ms to 33 ms, confirmed on a rerun, starting at commit 72802a9 ("Show each line's product name on an order"). That commit adds a third sequential store round trip (productNames) to every detail request. The k6 script perf/orders.js gets scenario-tagged thresholds at the baseline plus 20%, so it fails under load until the endpoint is fast again. The defect is recorded and filed.
inScope: Thresholds on http_req_duration{scenario:detail} p(95) and p(99) in perf/orders.js, added beside the existing thresholds; no existing scenario, check or threshold changes
Recording and filing the detail slowdown
outOfScope: Changing application code to win the time back (a person's job)
list p99 and search p99: their baselines vary too much (cv 10.6% and 9.6%) to judge, and neither was a slowdown
Restructuring perf/orders.js beyond adding the thresholds and the ticket tag comment
assumptions: The thresholds come from the baselines in the work item (p95 22 ms and p99 23 ms) plus the run's 20% headroom: p(95)<26.4 and p(99)<27.6.
The existing global thresholds (http_req_failed rate<0.01, http_req_duration p(95)<2000) stay unchanged.
run_tests runs smoke mode with thresholds off, so it shows that the script still runs. It doesn't enforce the new thresholds.

risks.description: Thresholds at baseline + 20% may fail on slower CI hardware than TestForge's measuring environment
risks.mitigation: The thresholds are tagged to the detail scenario only, and the baseline variance was small (cv 1.6–2.1%)

acceptanceCriteria.text: The detail scenario of perf/orders.js holds p95 http_req_duration below 26.4 ms (baseline 22 ms + 20%)
The detail scenario of perf/orders.js holds p99 http_req_duration below 27.6 ms (baseline 23 ms + 20%)

testCases.title: detail scenario keeps p95 and p99 latency within 20% of the last good runs
steps: Run perf/orders.js under its constant-arrival-rate scenarios
testCases.expected: Thresholds pass when the detail latency is at baseline. They fail now (p95 30 ms, p99 33 ms) until the extra round trip is removed.
testCases.rationale: Commit 72802a9 added productNames(), a separate awaited store query on every GET /orders/:id after findOrder and orderLines. That takes the request from 2 sequential round trips (6–9 ms each) to 3, about +8 ms, which matches the measured slowdown. The commit message says the names come 'in one query with the lines', but the code makes a separate query.

strategy.environmentNotes: The orders API (npm start) is served at BASE_URL, default http://localhost:4310.

defects.title: Order detail (GET /orders/:id) p95/p99 latency up ~40% since 72802a9: extra store round trip for product names
defects.description: The perf/orders.js detail scenario's p95 latency rose from 22 ms to 30 ms (+40.7%, 31 ms on the rerun). Its p99 rose from 23 ms to 33 ms (+39.6%, 33 ms on the rerun). The baseline is the median of 5 good runs (cv 1.6–2.1%). The bisect's first slow commit is 72802a9fba0d, "Show each line's product name on an order". That commit adds `productNames()` in src/store.js, a separate awaited query (`roundTrip()`, 6–9 ms) that the order route in src/app.js calls after `findOrder` and `orderLines`. Each detail request now makes 3 sequential round trips instead of 2, which matches the ~8 ms increase. The commit message says the names come "in one query with the lines", but the code queries for them separately. The fix is to return the product name from `orderLines` (where it already looks up each line's product for the price) and drop the extra query. The new thresholds are 'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}': p(95)<26.4, p(99)<27.6 (baseline + 20%), and they will fail under load until this is fixed.
defects.evidence: Work item measurements: detail p95 22→30 ms (rerun 31), p99 23→33 ms (rerun 33). Bisect: first failed at 72802a9fba0d. Diff: src/app.js adds `const names = await productNames(items.map(...))`; src/store.js productNames() awaits roundTrip().
